title: Teddy Lehman's 2003 Bednarik and Butkus Award Sweep
question: Which Oklahoma linebacker won the Bednarik Award and Butkus Award in 2003?
answer: Linebacker Teddy Lehman won the Chuck Bednarik Award on Dec. 11, 2003, and the Butkus Award the next night. He was OU's first Bednarik winner and gave the Sooners a fourth Butkus Award.
summary: Teddy Lehman won the 2003 Bednarik Award and Butkus Award on back-to-back nights, OU's first Bednarik and its fourth Butkus, the most of any program then.
body: Teddy Lehman had quite a week in December 2003. On Thursday night, Dec. 11, the Oklahoma senior linebacker won the Chuck Bednarik Award as the nation's top defensive player. On Friday night in Orlando, he added the Butkus Award as the country's best linebacker. It is still the only Bednarik Award in Oklahoma history.

The Bednarik announcement came during the Home Depot college football awards show, and Lehman beat out his own teammate, defensive tackle Tommie Harris, along with Florida State linebacker Michael Boulware. For the Butkus, he topped Texas' Derrick Johnson and Miami's Jonathan Vilma. It was Lehman's second straight year as a Butkus finalist, and the win gave OU four Butkus Awards, the most by any program at the time, joining Brian Bosworth's two and Rocky Calmus' 2001 trophy.

The Fort Gibson native earned it. He led the Sooners in tackles for a second straight season with 109, and OU's defense finished the regular season ranked first nationally in total defense. He was named Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year by the league's coaches and made the FWAA, AFCA and Walter Camp All-America teams for the second consecutive year. Against UCLA he posted a career-high 17 tackles and an interception.

Lehman was no stranger to big moments. As a sophomore in 2001, he was the player who caught the ball that Roy Williams knocked loose from Texas quarterback Chris Simms on the famous Superman play and took it in for a touchdown.
The Detroit Lions drafted Lehman in the second round in 2004. Today he is a familiar voice to Sooner fans as a color analyst on OU football radio broadcasts.
